title: Results Excerpt — Section Audit
subject: solver-log claims audited against the supplied evidence
summary: A synthetic Results excerpt reporting solver outcomes across 12 instances, audited against the exact solver-log evidence supplied. The excerpt's absolute optimality, timing, and deployment-readiness statements are checked against the reported per-instance outcomes; no external timing, deployment, or certificate evidence was supplied beyond these solver logs.
footer: This HTML is a presentation of the canonical text audit and adds no finding, number, or correction beyond it.

findings.title: Universal optimality claim contradicted by the excerpt's own counts
findings.source: The optimizer always returns the global optimum within 10 s.
findings.evidence: The same excerpt reports that only 9 of 12 runs ended with solver status OPTIMAL; 3 runs reached the 60 s time limit with feasible incumbents and final gaps of 4.1%, 5.3%, and 7.8%, which are not certified optima.
findings.consequence: The universal claim is directly contradicted by the excerpt's own reported outcomes: 3 of 12 instances did not return a certified global optimum.
findings.correction: Replace the universal claim with the reported split: 9 of 12 instances reached solver status OPTIMAL under a 1% relative MIP-gap tolerance, and 3 of 12 reached the 60 s time limit with feasible incumbents at gaps of 4.1%, 5.3%, and 7.8%.

findings.title: Unsupported 10 s timing figure
findings.source: The optimizer always returns the global optimum within 10 s.
findings.evidence: No solve-time measurement of 10 s appears anywhere in the supplied evidence. The only timing figure given is the 60 s limit reached by 3 of 12 runs.
findings.consequence: The 10 s figure is not derivable from the supplied solver logs and would present a fabricated timing value as a measured result.
findings.correction: Remove the 10 s figure unless the author supplies the actual per-instance or aggregate solve-time measurements it is meant to summarize.

findings.title: Deployment-readiness claim exceeds the solver-log evidence
findings.source: The method is therefore ready for real-time deployment.
findings.evidence: The supplied evidence is limited to solver status, MIP-gap, and time-limit outcomes across 12 instances. No deployment experiment, exact-optimality certificate for all instances, or timing measurement outside these solver logs is supplied.
findings.consequence: The excerpt converts a finite, partly time-limited solver-log evaluation into a general real-time deployment-readiness conclusion, including for the 3 instances that did not reach a certified optimum.
findings.correction: Remove the deployment-readiness statement. State only the reported solver outcomes and request deployment-relevant evidence (timing under operational constraints, a deployment trial) as an author query before any readiness claim is made.

findings.title: Missing reproducibility and instance-set detail
findings.source: Across 12 instances, 9 runs ended with solver status OPTIMAL under a 1% relative MIP-gap tolerance, while 3 reached the 60 s time limit with feasible incumbents and final gaps of 4.1%, 5.3%, and 7.8%.
findings.evidence: The excerpt gives instance counts, solver status, MIP-gap tolerance, and time limit, but no solver identity or version, hardware, seeds, or a description of what the 12 instances are drawn from.
findings.consequence: Without solver identity, hardware, and instance-set composition, the reported outcomes cannot be independently reconstructed or checked for configuration bias.
findings.correction: Request the solver name and version, hardware, seeds, and instance-set source/composition as an external author query; do not infer or insert these details.
